answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make each identity pay a real, non-refundable cost before it can earn. A hollow account farm stops being profitable when every new identity must spend compute on a fresh proof of work, so one operator cannot spin up thousands of agents for free. Rewards then flow only to identities that did real work, and by the time the first orchard of rewards ripens at dawn, the cheap fakes have already run out of money.
